claims.text: NCEI quality-controls GHCN-Daily on every reprocessing: a format-checking program first sets malformed records to missing, then a fully automated suite of QA tests (Durre et al. 2010) flags values; NCEI says about 0.3% of nearly 2 billion values are flagged, 98-99% of them true errors.

evidence.passage: During each reprocessing cycle, the data are first passed through a "format checking program" that looks for such problems as impossible months or days, invalid characters in data fields, etc. If this occurs, then the routine sets the offending records to missing.
This system flags approximately 0.3% of nearly 2 billion data values. It is estimated that 98-99% of the values flagged are true data errors and only 1-2% are false positives (Durre et al. 2010).
This paper describes a comprehensive set of fully automated quality assurance (QA) procedures for ob-

GHCN-Daily is comprised of daily climate records from numerous sources that have been integrated and subjected to a common suite of quality assurance reviews. … reconstructed each weekend from its 25-plus data source components to ensure that GHCN-Daily is generally in sync with its growing list of constituent sources. During this process, the system applies quality assurance checks to the full dataset.

Every day there are updates to GHCN-Daily station data from a variety of data streams, which also undergo a suite of quality checks. In addition the dataset is reconstructed each weekend from its 25-plus data source components to ensure that GHCN-Daily is generally in sync with its growing list of constituent sources. During this process, the system applies quality assurance checks to the full dataset.

The process of integrating data from multiple sources into GHCNd takes place in three steps: | - Screening the source data for stations whose identity is unknown or questionable | - Classifying each station in a source dataset either as one that is already represented in GHCNd or as a new site | - Mingling the data from the different sources | The process performs the first two of these steps whenever a new source dataset or additional stations become available, while the mingling of data is part of the automated processing that creates GHCNd on a regular basis. … Mingling takes place according to a hierarchy of data sources and in a manner that attempts to maximize the amount of data included while also minimizing the degree to which data from sources with different characteristics are mixed. … Data from the Global Summary of the Day dataset are used only if no observations are available from any other source for that station, month, and element.

Daily data from GHCN are available as individual ASCII (i.e., plain text) files (one file per station) and as a GZIP-compressed TAR file containing all of the station files. … ## Access Methods | - HTTPS | - Climate Data Online
Generally, real-time replacement of updated data streams are replaced by archive-ready data sources 45 to 60 days after the end of a month.

Each individual check in the GHCN-Daily QA system | is required to have a false-positive rate of no more than | 20%; that is, no more than one in five values flagged | is allowed to be a false positive.

claims.text: The checks are: trace-flag consistency, naught, duplicate, world-record exceedance (bounds), streak, frequent-value, gap, z-score and percentile climatological outliers, internal temperature consistency, temporal (spike/dip), lagged temperature range, pan-vs-air temperature, snow-temperature (warm), snowfall-to-snow-depth, snow-to-precipitation ratio, four spatial consistency checks, megaconsistency, and a date-based snow outlier check; each failure sets a one-letter QFLAG (D, G, I, K, L, M, N, O, R, S, T, W, X, Z).

evidence.passage: Checks for days on which maximum and minimum temperature are both equal to 0°C at stations not operated by the U.S. or are both equal to -17.8°C (0°F) at U.S. stations.
Checks for temperatures that differ greatly from a predicted value generated from a linear-regression-based estimate generated from neighboring values.

claims.text: Some source networks run their own QC before NCEI: CoCoRaHS combines automated form checks with manual daily review by headquarters staff and coordinators; NCEI's COOP Summary of the Day file (DSI-3210) carries flags from QC by NCDC personnel. GHCN-Daily then reruns its own automated QA on all of it.

evidence.passage: Users must be aware that DSI-3210 contains flagged data that have been quality controlled by personnel at the NCDC. DSI-3211 contains only automated quality controlled data.

1. Precipitation Checks | a. Trace flag consistency check … b. Bounds check – Identifies precipitation totals that exceed the world extreme for the highest 24-hour total ever observed. | d.
